primary_sources.locator: Open Science Collaboration, Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science, Science 349 (2015) aac4716, doi:10.1126/science.aac4716
primary_sources.pressure: Replication outcomes require protocol/sample/context tracking and do not reduce to binary truth labels.

primary_sources.locator: A. Franco, N. Malhotra and G. Simonovits, Publication bias in the social sciences: Unlocking the file drawer, Science 345 (2014) 1502–1505, doi:10.1126/science.1255484
primary_sources.pressure: Null/non-significant outcomes can be selectively hidden, so visibility/publication status is a load-bearing corpus coordinate.

primary_sources.locator: A. Gelman, X.-L. Meng and H. Stern, Posterior predictive assessment of model fitness via realized discrepancies, Statistica Sinica 6 (1996) 733–807
primary_sources.pressure: A discrepancy can diagnose model inadequacy without uniquely identifying one replacement or causal responsibility.

primary_sources.locator: Errington et al., Investigating the replicability of preclinical cancer biology, eLife 10 (2021) e71601, doi:10.7554/eLife.71601
primary_sources.pressure: Replication programs require feasibility/context/protocol distinctions and can yield mixed or non-identifying evidence rather than one global verdict.

rounds.challenge_neighborhood: software deployment + clinical harm + industrial accident

primary_sources.locator: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, In the Matter of Knight Capital Americas LLC, Exchange Act Release No. 70694 / Administrative Proceeding File No. 3-15570 (Oct. 16, 2013)
primary_sources.pressure: A software deployment/configuration failure combines execution defects, missing deployment controls, rapid material harm and concrete remediation.

primary_sources.pressure: An intervention can fail through excess clinical harm in a registered population while the inference remains molecule/regimen/context scoped.
